title: Mass-constrained hydrologic networks reveal a snow-storage limitation in a Colorado watershed
summary: Yihan Wang and colleagues at the University of Oklahoma, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, the International Computer Science Institute and the University of Michigan present PECAN, a distributed convolutional LSTM framework with strict and relaxed mass-conservation variants. In a snow-dominated Colorado watershed, the models produced competitive streamflow simulations and spatial latent states resembling reference soil-moisture dynamics. Comparison of strict and relaxed constraints revealed that the strict variant prematurely removed winter snow storage rather than retaining it for spring release. This is a single-basin proof of concept, without cross-basin validation.
organization: University of Oklahoma; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; International Computer Science Institute; University of Michigan

evidence.tested: The first arXiv version compares strict and relaxed mass-conserving distributed models with LSTM, MC-LSTM, MCR-LSTM and VIC baselines at two gauges; it compares latent states with SWE and soil-moisture references in the North Platte Headwaters watershed.
evidence.unknown: Single-basin proof of concept; no cross-basin validation. The strict model’s premature loss of winter snow storage is a limitation identified by the study.
evidence.ai_role: A convolutional LSTM models spatially distributed streamflow under strict or relaxed conservation constraints; interpreting internal states exposes a snow-storage mismatch.

source_review.scope: Primary source full text reviewed for title, authorship, Methods, Results, version date and stated limitations.
